boundary_decision.rationale: Both providers independently reached entry_kind=aggregate and both explicitly uphold the registry validation flag that a contract is not an organization. The boundary is the jointly owned multi-party agreement record composed of party positions, clause structure, deontic obligations and lifecycle events, with the legal entities, the procurement award process, adjudication proceedings, proprietary/title effects, insolvency and settlement execution held as neighbouring models. Claude's six sourced boundary notes and grok's CISG/HCCH sphere-of-application notes agree on every exclusion, so the boundary is settled before any node is accepted.

decisions.rationale: Claude has six sourced boundary notes naming concrete neighbour models, an explicit inline_only_rationale for every finding that mints no artifact, a sixteen-dimension coverage checklist with no self-declared gap, and separate findings for provenance, access, retention and interoperability. Grok is stronger on CISG article-level depth but declares a validation gap and lumps notices, dispute clauses, joint record, access and retention into one composite finding, which is the less clear boundary.
A genuine hole in the base: the agreed text can be addressed and ranked but not construed. CISG Articles 7-9 give it primary-source grounding and it duplicates nothing already present.

decisions.concept: Anticipatory breach, suspension, adequate assurance, Nachfrist
decisions.rationale: The base jumps from breach declaration to remedy election with no additional-period, suspension or assurance path. CISG Articles 47, 63, 71-73 support four distinct states the base cannot currently represent.

decisions.concept: Writing requirement, statute of frauds and Article 96 reservations
decisions.disposition: rejected as duplicative; deferred as question-level enrichment
decisions.rationale: The base finding execution-signature-and-form already owns the form-requirement decision surface. Adding grok's finding would create a second execution node overlapping on signature method. The CISG Article 11 versus UCC 2-201 versus Article 12/96 tension is recorded as a publication hold and deferred research item instead of new structure.

decisions.concept: Remedy catalogue detail (mitigation, substitute-transaction measure, Article 28 forum filter, restitution)
decisions.rationale: Base breach-excuse-and-remedy already carries remedy election and quantification against caps or liquidated sums, and termination-expiry-and-survival carries wind-down and final accounting. Grok's additions are measurement refinements inside an existing surface, not a missing surface.

decisions.disposition: rejected in favour of base decomposition
decisions.rationale: The base already separates notice-and-formal-communication, dispute-forum-and-enforceability, access-and-disclosure-control, retention-limitation-and-deletion and provenance-and-audit-trail. Importing a composite would blur four distinct governance decision surfaces the base keeps apart.

decisions.concept: Assignment, guarantees and third-party rights as one node
decisions.rationale: The base splits this correctly into third-party-positions (agents, guarantors, beneficiaries, subcontracting) and assignment-and-novation (transfer kind, consent, change of control, position continuity). Grok's single node would double-own both.

Base cla-q-machine-rule-link covers the rule-to-provision assertion and oac-q-standard-terms covers incorporation of competing form sets. Many-to-many isomorphism is a refinement of an existing question, not a new finding.

decisions.concept: Delivery, conformity, examination and seller cure
decisions.rationale: Base delivery-and-risk-transfer holds conformity and examination periods, performance-record-and-acceptance holds acceptance and rejection states, and milestone-and-due-condition holds cure periods. Grok's node restates all three.

Base del-q-risk-transfer covers the passing of risk and brm-q-excuse-ground covers impediment and hardship with evidence. CISG Article 80 self-caused failure is a worthwhile question-level addition but does not justify a parallel finding.

decisions.concept: Statutory default duties not created by a clause (CISG Articles 30, 53, 31, 55, 57-59)
decisions.rationale: Base obl-q-source-clause presumes a provision creates each duty, so gap-filled statutory duties currently have no source. This is a real modelling question about whether an obligation's source may be a legal norm rather than a clause, and it needs its own resolution rather than an imported node.

The base refuses to mint artifacts for derived readings of clause text (payment terms, protective terms, milestones, termination state) to prevent a second normatively significant copy of the executed wording. This discipline is preserved and grok's flatter artifact set is not merged.

decisions.concept: Incoterms trade terms and risk-transfer point
decisions.rationale: Grok has no trade-term source at all; the base grounds delivery, cost allocation and the named place in ICC Incoterms 2020, which is required for any goods-sale profile.

decisions.concept: eIDAS and Data Act sourced elements
decisions.rationale: Signature assurance levels, trust-service concepts and unfair-term controls in the base come from EU instruments. They stay, marked as regional alignment rather than universal rule, consistent with grok's use of the UNCITRAL model laws as the cross-border baseline.

decisions.concept: National validity doctrines (mistake, fraud, duress, illegality)
decisions.rationale: CISG Article 4 excludes validity and both providers place it in a sibling or overlay. The base keeps only the assertion surface in effectiveness-conditions-and-validity, which is the correct minimum without importing grok's declared validation gap.

deferred_research: Fetch UCC Article 2 primary text beyond section 2-201 - specifically 2-207 battle of forms, 2-609 adequate assurance, and the 2-706/2-708/2-712/2-713 damages measures - to test whether the accepted anticipatory-breach finding holds under a second, non-CISG regime.

Resolve whether an obligation's source may be a legal norm rather than a clause, so that gap-filled statutory duties (CISG Articles 30, 53, 31, 55, 57-59) can be instantiated without a fabricated provision reference.
Ground statutory late-payment interest defaults in a verified primary source, or publish the interest-basis element explicitly as configuration with no jurisdictional default table.
Assess the 1974 UN Limitation Convention as amended in 1980 as a distinct time-bar instrument against the base retention and limitation-period questions.
Evaluate sector standard forms (ISDA Master, FIDIC, GAFTA, BIMCO) and insurance policies as EXTEND profiles, and confirm the base carries the extension points those profiles would need.

Compare eIDAS qualified-signature presumptions, UETA/ESIGN state enactments and the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Signatures reliability test to determine whether a single cross-regional signature assurance scale is defensible.

Decide whether set-off, plurality of obligors and transfer of obligations (UNIDROIT Chapters 8, 9, 11) belong in the accepted transfer surface or in a sibling model, since neither provider currently owns set-off.
Specify the smart-contract execution substrate boundary: whether self-executing performance is evidence of performance only, or requires its own recorded execution state.
publication_holds: Source verification hold: none of the 16 base URLs or the 5 grok-only URLs were re-fetched in this adjudication. Every accepted source must be resolved live and version-pinned before publication, with particular attention to the two different LegalRuleML OS URLs, Akoma Ntoso naming-convention v1.0 versus core v1.0 Part 1, UBL 2.4 Committee Specification status, Incoterms 2020, and eIDAS 'as amended by the European Digital Identity framework'.

Multi-profile validation hold: the merged structure must be exercised against at least three domain profiles before publication - an international CISG sale of goods, a domestic US goods sale where UCC Article 2 and the section 2-201 writing rule apply, and a services or framework-plus-call-off agreement where no goods and no executed single instrument exist.

Writing-rule hold: CISG Article 11 (no writing required), CISG Articles 12 and 96 reservations, and UCC section 2-201 must be carried as co-recorded competing rules with the reservation state per party place of business. Do not publish a single resolved writing rule.

Regional-labelling hold: eIDAS signature assurance levels and the Data Act unfair-term and smart-contract essential-requirement material are EU-regional and must be published as regional alignments, not universal rules, alongside the technology-neutral UNCITRAL reliability test.

No-conformance hold: alignments to UBL, LegalRuleML, Akoma Ntoso, PROV-O and RFC 3339 are declared alignments only. Publication must state the claim level and must not assert tested conformance for any instance without test evidence.
